$comment: Constructors of ONE priority run in the units' input order, then each unit's definition order -- one rule for every format (src/link/static_init_tables.hpp states the decision, its measurement and what it refuses). The link's input is main.c u1.c u2.c u3.c w.c; `w` prototypes `wc` before it defines `wa` and `wb`, so its own numbering puts `wc` first and an order taken from ids runs it first. The stdout is the order (each constructor notes its number), the exit code the count (six ran). The twin `constructor_ties_run_in_input_then_definition_order_reversed` links the same units in the opposite order; the unit-tier pins are tests/link/test_constructor_order_through_the_link.cpp and tests/link/test_static_init_schedule.cpp. FOUR TARGETS: pe runs natively on the Windows gate host, elf x86_64 + arm64 under qemu on Linux, macho on darwin.
